specification.title: Explicit transaction: catch a unique violation, then commit
steps: Begin a transaction with the framework's explicit transaction API.
Write the marker `tx` and make sure the write was sent.
Insert the duplicate value 'taken' into uniq. Catch the unique violation. Send nothing else.
Checkpoint `before-end`: report the same backend PID. Send no query.
Checkpoint `after-api` as soon as that call has returned, before any reuse.
Run one new transaction that writes `reuse`. Checkpoint `reuse-after-write` if it starts.
Checkpoint `after-end`, as soon as the case function has returned.

invariants.statement: The run recorded the application-visible outcome and an independent database outcome that agree with each other. This invariant does not judge whether the application-visible outcome was the correct commit report. That judgment is in the research summary.

execution.description: DriverManagerDataSource. A connection is opened for the transaction and closed when Spring releases it. No pool. The outer TransactionTemplate uses the default PROPAGATION_REQUIRED. A nested TransactionTemplate uses PROPAGATION_NESTED. TX-03 is not run in this mode (not-applicable-by-design). On this server, DataSourceUtils.releaseConnection closed a connection whose autocommit was false, and that backend was gone from pg_stat_activity. DataSourceTransactionManager.doCleanupAfterCompletion unbinds the holder and then calls releaseConnection, which closes the connection because it is no longer bound. The next TransactionTemplate ran on a different backend. This DataSource cannot hand a transactionally active connection to later work.
execution.form: PlatformTransactionManager.getTransaction, catch DataAccessException, manager.commit. Writes use JdbcTemplate.

server.version: PostgreSQL 18.6 (Debian 18.6-1.pgdg13+2) on aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu, compiled by gcc (Debian 14.2.0-19) 14.2.0, 64-bit

fault.mechanism: A unique_violation raised by PostgreSQL inside the transaction, and caught by the application. The application then calls the explicit commit API.
fault.injection_point: After the first write, before the explicit commit.
fault.expected_server: The failed statement aborts the transaction. No savepoint is created.
fault.expected_client: The application catches 23505 and calls commit.

knowledge: The application caught the unique violation and then called the framework's commit method.

api_outcome.contract: Spring Framework 7.0.9 TransactionTemplate.execute (org.springframework.transaction.support.TransactionTemplate) calls PlatformTransactionManager.commit only when the callback returns, and on a RuntimeException or Error it rolls the transaction back and rethrows that same throwable. The 7.0.9 reference, Rolling Back a Declarative Transaction, states the default rule: "In its default configuration, the Spring Framework's transaction infrastructure code marks a transaction for rollback only in the case of runtime, unchecked exceptions. That is, when the thrown exception is an instance or subclass of RuntimeException. (Error instances also, by default, result in a rollback)." The default tx:advice settings say: "Any RuntimeException triggers rollback, and any checked Exception does not." No custom rollback rule is installed. The nested TransactionTemplate uses PROPAGATION_NESTED. The 7.0.9 reference, Understanding PROPAGATION_NESTED, states: "PROPAGATION_NESTED uses a single physical transaction with multiple savepoints that it can roll back to. Such partial rollbacks let an inner transaction scope trigger a rollback for its scope, with the outer transaction being able to continue the physical transaction despite some operations having been rolled back. This setting is typically mapped onto JDBC savepoints, so it works only with JDBC resource transactions." DataSourceTransactionManager's class javadoc states: "This transaction manager supports nested transactions via the JDBC Savepoint mechanism." Explicit form: getTransaction returns a TransactionStatus and the application calls commit.

violation.message: PreparedStatementCallback; SQL [insert into uniq (code) values (?)]; ERROR: duplicate key value violates unique constraint "uniq_code_key" Detail: Key (code)=(taken) already exists.

evaluation.mechanism_detail: at before-end the session was "idle in transaction (aborted)"; at after-api the session had closed
evaluation.reason: PR-01.1 held: the API reported committed; at before-end the session was "idle in transaction (aborted)"; at after-api the session had closed

preconditions.description: the write of marker "tx" had reached PostgreSQL at `after-write` (a row lock on item, in pg_locks)
a unique_violation (23505) was observed on the failing statement
the marker visibility agrees with pg_xact_status() for the captured transaction
